name: Trattenbachtal & Trattenbachalm
kurzbeschreibung: The Trattenbachtal in the Kitzbühel Alps is a tranquil alpine valley in the Hohe Salve region featuring traditional dairy pastures, clear mountain streams, and Kröndlhorn views.
preis: Trails freely accessible; local toll road into Kelchsau approx. €4-6 per vehicle
oeffnungszeiten: Hiking paths accessible May to October; alpine cheese huts open June through September
beschreibung:
Überblick

The wonderfully serene Trattenbachtal is cradled within the rolling grassy ridges of the Kitzbühel Alps, forming an untouched tributary valley of the Brixental in the Hohe Salve holiday region near Hopfgarten. Encircled by majestic peaks such as Mount Kröndlhorn (2,444 m) and Schwaigberghorn, this secluded high sanctuary has preserved authentic centuries-old alpine pastoral traditions. The rushing waters of the crystal Trattenbach brook provide soothing soundtracks and refreshing gravel eddies during warm summer afternoons. Trattenbachtal is celebrated as an insider gem for walkers seeking tranquility far removed from commercial tourism. Verdant pastures dotted with aromatic alpine flora, pine woods, and grazing Tyrolean cattle define the landscape. Traditional log huts including the Trattenbachalm welcome hikers during summer with hand-churned alpine cheese, raw buttermilk, and cold cuts.

Route & Anforderungen

The journey through the Trattenbachtal commences at the trailhead in the Kelchsau valley (Kurzer Grund fork) and follows a gently ascending forest road flanking the brook up to the Trattenbachalm hut (approx. five kilometres, 1.5 to 2 hours one way, 350 m elevation gain). For committed peak-baggers, the hut serves as the spring-board for climbing Mount Kröndlhorn, whose summit hosts the highest mountain chapel in the Kitzbühel Alps (additional 2.5 hours, sure-footedness essential). The valley track is broad and well-packed, making it suitable for all-terrain prams and gravel cyclists. Sturdy walking shoes with gripping tread are recommended.

Besuch & Anreise

Motorists travel via the Inntal motorway A12 (exit Wörgl Ost) and highway B170 to Hopfgarten, turning into the scenic Kelchsau side valley. Beyond the Kelchsau toll station, a paved lane leads into Kurzer Grund to the hiker car park. Rail passengers arrive at Hopfgarten station and take local hikers' shuttles.

Tipps

Take a seat on the weathered sun terrace of Trattenbachalm for a traditional cold meat-and-cheese platter ('Brettljause') complemented by artisanal mountain cheese and fresh buttermilk.
saison: Mai bis Oktober (Almbewirtschaftung Mitte Juni bis Anfang Oktober)
